title: Design around the distance
standfirst: Flying between regions is not optional here; the country is too large for anything else.

blocks.heading: One region per week
paras: The temptation is to link the Rockies and the coast by road. The drive is magnificent and it costs three days.
We fly between regions and drive within them, which buys back most of a week on a fortnight's trip.

blocks.heading: The last leg by air
blocks.caption: Float plane or helicopter into the lodges.
paras: The wilderness lodges worth reaching are not on a road, and that is the point of them.
The final leg is a float plane or a helicopter, booked with the lodge rather than separately.

blocks.heading: Winter is a different country
blocks.caption: January to March for powder and northern light.
paras: The same regions in winter are quieter, emptier and in some ways better, and almost nobody asks for them.
Guides and cat-skiing book a year ahead, so winter is planned in the spring before.

blocks.heading: Questions members ask
blocks.intro: The ones that come up nearly every time.

a: June to September for the Rockies and the coast; January to March for powder and the northern lights.
Fourteen nights for two regions. Ten is possible for one.
Among the best. The lodges are set up for it and the distances within a region are manageable.

blocks.heading: We are ready when you are
paras: Every itinerary starts with a conversation about what you actually want from the days, and works backwards to houses, guides and timing from there.
